content.intended_use: Prove the necessary cost of deterministic finite-sum optimization

map: Normalize gamma=B=1; use a quadratic chain with per-round component activation.
Choose directions orthogonal to prior queries and stop each round after ceil(m/2) distinct component indices.
Use a=sqrt(3/(k+1)),k=floor(1/sqrt(32 epsilon)),q=floor(k/2), and show truncated support has gap>=1/(32k²).
Check values/gradients/prox against the eventual fixed quadratic construction (Lemmas 4–5); apply scaling.
proofs.omitted_details: The full proof is not stored locally; the map serves only as a locator and cannot certify an independent proof.
proofs.reading_coverage: Theorem 3 and B.3 including calibration and prox-consistency argument; not an independent proof review.

assumptions: m>=2; gamma,B>0; each f_i convex gamma-smooth.
Deterministic adaptive h_F algorithm; dimension not fixed in advance.
statement.conclusion: Omega(m sqrt(gamma B²/epsilon)) component-oracle calls in the stated small-accuracy window.
statement.objects_and_definitions: F=(1/m)sum_i f_i; X=B_2(B); h_F combines component value, gradient and prox_{f_i}(x,beta)=argmin_{u in X}{f_i(u)+(beta/2)||u-x||²}. The constructed quadratic functions are defined on all R^d.
statement.parameter_domains: 0<epsilon<gamma B²/128. This is the explicit Appendix B.3 calibration window; the printed theorem has a broader statement.
statement.quantifiers_and_randomness: For every deterministic adaptive A, there exist d=O(m sqrt(gamma B²/epsilon)) and a consistent fixed collection of components such that obtaining any output xhat with F(xhat)-min_X F<epsilon requires the stated worst-case calls.
